title: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
summary: Svix response to the October, 2026 weak CA certificates issued by eMudhra
body_markdown:
Svix's information security team is aware of dangerously-weak intermediate CA certificates issued by the certification authority eMudhra, as described in[this branded security release](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/) and[this bugzilla thread](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2083449) .


The issue affects everyone on the internet, Svix included, and could be used by a network-privileged attacker to issue malicious TLS certificates and intercept traffic.


New images have been released which distrust the Root CAs which signed the affected certificates (emSign ECC Root CA - G3 and Comodo AAA Services) and incorporate the latest versions of[rustls-webpki](https://github.com/rustls/webpki) to block any certificate trust chains that go through one of the affected certificates.


Cloud users are already protected. Open-source customers should upgrade to[Svix Server v1.102.1](https://github.com/svix/svix-webhooks/releases/tag/server-v1.102.1) . Bridge users should upgrade to[Bridge v1.101.0](https://github.com/svix/svix-webhooks/releases/tag/bridge-v1.101.0) . On-premises Svix Enterprise users using Helm should upgrade to 1.3114. Users of the Svix SDK should use their programming language's package manage to ensure that relevant dependencies are upgraded (e.g.,` certifi` on Python), and should make sure that their operating systems and/or container base images have the latest` ca-certificates` packages.


If you have any questions or concerns, please don't hesitate to reach out tosupport@svix.com .
